messages:
ashley: FYI seeing a spike of gRPC streams failing with short 503/Unavailable at the edge in eu-west-1 since ~03:40 UTC. A lot of client sessions get cut after ~55-65s. No LB config changed in last 48h AFAIK.
ashley: Example from the client side: 
```
rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: received unexpected EOS
level=warn grpc_stream: stream closed prematurely, duration=58s
```
micah: Any pattern on which routes or model backends? all models or a subset?
ashley: Mostly long-running chat streams -> streaming completions. Short gen (single response) unaffected. Also noticed higher rate from a few k8s nodes that do egress through the same NAT gateway.
raj: Could be ALB/CloudLB idle timeout or GOAWAY from the edge. ALBs terminate HTTP/2 and convert to HTTP/1 upstream in our setup; windowing or buffer clamping might drop long streams. What are the LB idle and backend keepalive settings?
ashley: ALB idle timeout is default 60s. Backend keepalive (envoy->upstream) set to 120s. We saw the resets ~58-62s which smells like the ALB.
micah: ALB default 60s kills idle connections. Streaming gRPC must keep activity or use pings. We previously worked around by enabling HTTP2 pings from envoy. Did we enable GOAWAY logging?
ashley: Not currently. I'll turn on GOAWAY/stream logs in envoy.
netops-bot: deploy:edge-proxy v3.14 rolled to us-east-1 and eu-west-1 4d ago (no rollback). No config changes to AWS ALB from infra side.
raj: Also check NAT ephemeral ports exhaustion — if many outbound connections are short-lived, the NAT can start reusing tuples and confuse connection mapping. How many concurrent egress sockets on those nodes?
ashley: Node-level metric: egress connections peaked ~34k on two nodes. We usually see <8k.
micah: That's suspicious. If ephemeral ports are exhausted you can get connection resets as SNAT tables get saturated. Add a quick check: `ss -tn sport = :443 | wc -l` on the node and `sudo conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l`.
raj: Also capture a pcap at the node hitting the ALB with filter `tcp port 443 and host <ALB_IP>` and look for FIN/RST sequence and TLS alert frames. If we see ALB sending GOAWAY that confirms LB idle. If we see RST from NAT, that's different.
ashley: Running tcpdump + h2dump now. If it's ALB idle, options: 1) set ALB idle timeout higher (but ALB docs warn about long timeouts), 2) enable envoy keepalive/pings, 3) use dedicated NLB passthrough for long streams.
sre-oncall: FYI we already have an open ticket with AWS about edge ALB HTTP2 truncation behavior; they admitted a bug in specific ALB firmware in late 2025. Not sure if that variant is in our region.
micah: Quick mitigation: configure envoy to send HTTP/2 PING frames every 25s for streaming routes; that'll keep the ALB from considering the stream idle. Also set `upstream_idle_timeout` lower than ALB to force reconnect before ALB does.
ashley: Trying PINGs now on a canary route. Will report back in 15m.
raj: Also can we route streaming traffic via our edge NLB to avoid ALB HTTP2 termination? That would preserve h2 to upstream and remove translation issues. Cost/ops tradeoff though.
ashley: Agreed. If PING can stable it, we'll keep ALB. If not, plan B is NLB for /v1/stream endpoints.
micah: Also add a small load-test simulating sustained streaming opens to repro (we may be hitting a combination of ALB idle + NAT port reuse). I can drop a k6 script.
ashley: Action list: @raj capture pcaps + check NAT conntrack, @micah produce load test, I'm enabling h2 PINGs and GOAWAY logs. If anyone sees client-side TLS alerts or ALB GOAWAY logs, paste them here. :mag: 
raj: On it. I'll post captures and a quick tcpdump timeline.
ashley: Thanks — will update when canary confirms. :thumbsup:
